title: Etale sum extension preserves flat sheaves and K-flat complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $u:U\to X$ a separated etale morphism of finite type of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and the sheafified sum extension $u_{\Sigma!}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. If $F$ is a flat module sheaf on $U$, then $u_{\Sigma!}F$ is flat on $X$, where flat means that tensoring with the sheaf preserves exact sequences [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. If $P$ is an arbitrary unbounded K-flat cochain complex on $U$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex], then its degreewise sum extension $u_{\Sigma!}P$ is K-flat on $X$. Here K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In particular, if $P$ is K-flat and every $P^n$ is flat, then $u_{\Sigma!}P$ is K-flat with flat terms. There are no boundedness, constructibility, Noetherian, or finiteness hypotheses on the coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), canonical tensor-generator construction and sheaf projection isomorphism; agent expansion of its passage to unbounded total tensor complexes and the definition of K-flatness, rather than a verbatim assertion of this lemma.

proof.text: To prove flatness, let 0 \to G' \to G \to G'' \to 0 be a short exact sequence of A-module sheaves on X. The canonical projection isomorphisms of [lem-pur-etale-sheaf-projection-map] identify the tensor of this sequence with u_{\Sigma!}(F\otimes_Au^*(-)) term by term. The inverse-image functor u^*=u^{-1} is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so the sequence after u^* is exact; tensoring it with F is exact by the definition of flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Finally u_{\Sigma!} is exact on sheaves of modules over the constant ring A by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (u is etale). The definition of flatness tests G\mapsto G\otimes_A u_{\Sigma!}F; the symmetry isomorphism G\otimes_A u_{\Sigma!}F\cong u_{\Sigma!}F\otimes_A G, natural in G, and likewise u^*G\otimes_AF\cong F\otimes_Au^*G, move between the two orders, and a sequence naturally isomorphic to an exact one is exact. Therefore tensoring with u_{\Sigma!}F preserves this short exact sequence, and hence u_{\Sigma!}F is flat.

source.place: Tag 0GKF, lemma-f-shriek-projection, pure-tensor construction and stalkwise isomorphism

proof.text: Let B be any acyclic complex of A-module sheaves on X. Exactness of u^*=u^{-1} implies that u^*B is acyclic: in each degree it preserves the kernels and images defining the cohomology sheaf, so the induced homology sheaves remain zero. By [lem-pur-etale-sum-tensor-totalization], the canonical totalization isomorphism gives\n$$\operatorname{Tot}((u_{\Sigma!}P)\otimes_A B)\cong u_{\Sigma!}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_Au^*B).$$\nThe definition [def-pc-kflat-complex] puts the acyclic complex in the first factor. For complexes K, L the signed symmetry x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x on K^p\otimes_AL^q is an isomorphism of complexes \operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_AL)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_AK): with d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^px\otimes dy both composites send x\otimes y to (-1)^{pq}(dy\otimes x+(-1)^qy\otimes dx). Hence the K-flatness of P makes \operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_Au^*B)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(u^*B\otimes_AP) acyclic, and exactness of u_{\Sigma!} on module sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], applied degreewise, commutes with taking cohomology sheaves and so preserves that acyclicity. Thus \operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_Au_{\Sigma!}P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}((u_{\Sigma!}P)\otimes_AB) is acyclic for every acyclic B, which is exactly that u_{\Sigma!}P is K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0GKF, lemma-f-shriek-projection, together with the definition of K-flatness; unbounded totalization is the agent expansion recorded in the item source

proof.text: The degreewise extension of P has term (u_{\Sigma!}P)^n=u_{\Sigma!}(P^n) by the definition of the degreewise sum extension. If every P^n is flat, applying the flat-sheaf argument of the first step to each P^n shows that every u_{\Sigma!}(P^n) is flat. Combining this with the K-flatness proved in the second step gives the final assertion that u_{\Sigma!}P is K-flat with flat terms.
